source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 214: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 214: choose TP or PP only after measurement; the supplied prompt contains no platform facts, so the result is unresolved rather than a universal recommendation. Assume the model graph and layer shapes, precision, parameter/activation memory, GPU count/type and usable HBM (GiB), interconnect topology/bandwidth, software versions and clocks, request-length/arrival distributions, concurrency, batching, and latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability SLOs are recorded, with estimates labeled. Enumerate feasible TP degrees and balanced PP stage partitions, rejecting configurations without positive per-GPU memory headroom. Hypothesis: on identical hardware and a fixed representative workload, the feasible option with lower held-out p99 end-to-end latency while meeting every SLO gate is superior; falsify this if p99 is not lower or any gate fails. Randomize paired trials after warm-up, tune only on a separate set, and evaluate on held-out requests while holding workload mix, arrival rate, precision, clocks, concurrency, and batch policy constant. Measure compute, TP collectives or PP activation transfers, synchronization wait, stage imbalance, pipeline-bubble fraction, queueing, throughput, TTFT, TPOT, p50/p95/p99 latency, errors, quality, availability, memory headroom, and recovery time with units and uncertainty. TP can reduce per-GPU memory but adds frequent topology- and straggler-sensitive collectives; PP can reduce collectives but needs balanced stages and enough microbatches and incurs bubbles, transfers, and queueing. Control thermal/software drift and request mix. Run failure/reconfiguration tests only when authorized, isolated, bounded, redacted, and reversible. Canary the winner and roll back if held-out p99 or error/quality/availability thresholds regress, headroom vanishes, or recovery exceeds budget; require domain-expert review before treating this provisional calibration as authoritative.
